findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === never match
findings.body: At line 114 the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a full-day unavailable date override. `===` on objects compares references, so two separately created Dayjs instances are never equal. The branch never runs, `dateOverrideExist` becomes true but `find` returns falsy, and the function falls through to `return true`. A day marked unavailable by a date override is therefore reported as available, including for fixed hosts in round-robin events, allowing bookings that should be blocked.

findings.title: Working-hours check ignores duration and inverts multi-block logic
findings.body: The `workingHours.find` check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+minute`, ignoring `eventLength` and `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside but ends outside working hours passes. It also returns true if ANY block does not contain the slot, instead of checking if NO block contains it. With two blocks on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon) a valid slot inside one block is outside the other and is marked unavailable, while a weekday with no matching `days` entry returns falsy and is treated as available. Fixed hosts can appear available when they have no hours and unavailable when they have split hours.

findings.title: Date-override containment misses end overrun and exact boundary
findings.body: The override test only rejects a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`. It never checks `slotEndTime > overrideEnd`, and uses `isAfter` instead of same-or-after for the end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 10:00-11:00, slot 10:30-11:30) does not match either condition, `find` returns falsy, and with `dateOverrideExist=true` the function returns true. Bookings can extend beyond the override window, and a slot starting exactly at override end is also considered inside.

findings.title: Date-override day match mixes local and UTC timezones
findings.body: `utcOffset` is derived with `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()*-1` then applied to `dayjs(date.start)` which is parsed in server-local time, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`. Formatting both with `YYYY MM DD` compares a local-calendar day to a UTC-calendar day. Unless the server runs in UTC the day equality and the shifted start/end comparisons can be off by a day, causing overrides to apply to the wrong date or be ignored for organizers/invitees in other zones.

findings.title: Offsets derived from Date.toString() parsing are fragile
findings.body: Organizer and invitee offsets are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(zone).utcOffset()`. `Date.toString()` is locale and server-timezone dependent (e.g. includes local abbrev) and is not a stable input for dayjs parsing with a zone. It can parse incorrectly or yield Invalid Date/NaN, producing NaN start/end minutes and dropping all slots or shifting them. It should use `dayjs(override.start).tz(zone)` directly without stringifying.

findings.title: Active override filtered by wall-encoded instant not true instant
findings.body: The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` uses the stored override Date directly, but that Date encodes organizer wall time as UTC hours. The true UTC instant is wall minus organizer offset. Near midnight a wall time and its true instant fall on different invitee calendar days (e.g. true 23:30 UTC with +5:30 organizer becomes 05:00 wall next day). The override can then be attached to the wrong invitee day or missed entirely for invitees in distant timezones.

findings.title: Availability check ignores variable duration
findings.body: Slots are generated with `eventLength: input.duration || eventType.length` but `availabilityCheckProps` hard-codes `eventLength: eventType.length`. For event types with multiple duration options the `checkIfIsAvailable` busy/override/working-hours window uses the wrong length, so a longer selected duration can be reported as available when it overruns an override, working hours, or busy block, or vice versa.
